title: Lesson Plan — Chemical Reactions and Equations (Class 10 CBSE Science)
subject: Science
objectives: Recognise indicators of a chemical reaction (colour change, gas, ppt, temperature).
Convert word equations into balanced chemical equations.
Balance chemical equations using the law of conservation of mass.
Classify reactions as combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, or redox.
Distinguish thermal, photochemical, and electrolytic decomposition.
Use reactivity series to predict displacement reactions.
Identify oxidation and reduction; explain corrosion and rancidity with prevention.
prerequisites: Concept of an atom and a molecule.
materials: Demonstration setup: Mg ribbon + tongs + lighter (for combustion demo)
Reagent bottles: dilute HCl, NaOH, AgNO₃, NaCl, FeSO₄, CuSO₄ (for displacement / double displacement demos)
Cards with reactions for a 'classify the type' card sort

activities.description: Demo: ignite a small piece of magnesium ribbon — show the bright white flame and the white powder of MgO. Ask: 'What evidence tells you a reaction has happened?'
student_actions: List indicators of reaction in their notebooks.

activities.description: Pair card sort: distribute 12 reaction cards (e.g. CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂; Fe + CuSO₄ → ...; AgNO₃ + NaCl → ...). Students sort into 5 bins (combination / decomposition / displacement / double displacement / redox).

Direct instruction in five blocks: (i) chemical equations + indicators; (ii) law of conservation of mass + balancing procedure (live example: Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂); (iii) the five reaction types with examples; (iv) thermal / photochemical / electrolytic decomposition + reactivity series for displacement; (v) corrosion + rancidity + prevention.
teacher_actions: Build a 5-step balancing checklist on the board.
Show a rusted nail and a galvanised one side-by-side.
student_actions: Predict products of one displacement reaction in pairs.

activities.description: Students do six worksheet questions: balancing, classification, predicting displacement, identifying oxidation/reduction, explaining a real-world rancidity scenario, designing a rust-prevention plan.
student_actions: Verify each balanced equation by counting atoms.

activities.description: Set homework: balance 5 given equations + write a paragraph on 'why food is packed in nitrogen'. Preview Chapter 2 (Acids, Bases and Salts) by showing a litmus paper colour change demo.

homework: Balance these 5 equations: (1) Al + O₂ → Al₂O₃; (2) NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + H₂O; (3) Pb(NO₃)₂ → PbO + NO₂ + O₂; (4) NH₃ + O₂ → NO + H₂O; (5) C₄H₁₀ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O.
Write a 5-sentence paragraph: 'Why are potato chips packed in bags filled with nitrogen?' Use the words rancidity, oxidation, antioxidant, oxygen.
Find one example each of combination, decomposition, and displacement reactions from your kitchen / home and write the chemical equation if you can.
assessment_ideas: Use the 6-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question quiz drawn from the chapter bank for next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on rust-prevention strategies using a 3-strategy + reasoning rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the homework paragraph using a vocabulary-usage rubric.
references: NCERT Class 10 Science textbook (jesc1dd), Chapter 1: Chemical Reactions and Equations.
